prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
New Labour because Britain deserves better. Our case is simple: Britain is a great country that can and must be better—one nation with shared values, merit before privilege, run for the many not the few. New Labour offers national renewal with drive, purpose and energy. We are a party of ideas and ideals, not outdated ideology: what counts is what works. Our objectives are radical; our means will be modern. This is our contract with the people—specific promises you can hold us to.

New Labour breaks from the old left and Conservative right. We have married enterprise with justice, modernised our party and our union link, and opened up policy and membership. Our values—equal worth, fairness, strong communities—are applied to the realities of a global economy.

Education is our number one priority: higher standards, not structures; class sizes of 30 or under for 5–7 year‑olds; nursery places for all four‑year‑olds; setting by ability; a National Grid for Learning; lifelong learning and a University for Industry. Over a Parliament, as we cut the costs of social failure, we will raise education’s share of national income.

We will promote personal prosperity for all through stability and prudence: low inflation, reformed and accountable monetary policy, strict fiscal rules (only borrow to invest), and sticking to current spending totals for two years. No increase in the basic or top rates of income tax; cut VAT on fuel to 5 per cent; a long‑term 10p starting rate; tax reform to promote saving and investment. Save to invest, not tax and spend. A windfall levy on excess utility profits will fund a welfare‑to‑work programme to get 250,000 under‑25s off benefit and into work.

We back business with a reformed, tougher competition law; revitalised public–private partnerships; support for small firms; science, design and green technologies; Regional Development Agencies; a sensibly set national minimum wage and basic workplace rights alongside flexibility; and union recognition where a majority vote for it. Our stakeholder economy links ambition with responsibility.

We will save and modernise the NHS: end the costly internal market, cut red tape and waiting lists, strengthen primary care, set tough quality targets, ban tobacco advertising, create an independent Food Standards Agency, and raise NHS spending in real terms each year, putting money into frontline care.

Tough on crime, tough on the causes of crime: halve the time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; streamline youth justice; put more police on the beat; decentralise the CPS; tackle disorder; strengthen victims’ rights; appoint an anti‑drugs supremo; and give Parliament a free vote to ban all handguns.

We will strengthen family life with a national childcare strategy, work–life balance rights, secure housing with reinvested council house receipts, action on homelessness, dignity in retirement with the basic pension protected and stakeholder pensions expanding second‑tier provision.

We will put the environment at the heart of government and deliver an integrated transport policy: improve the privatised railways in the public interest with a new rail authority and stronger regulation; a public–private partnership for the Tube; better buses; safer roads; cleaner vehicles; stewardship of the countryside; and support for arts, culture and sport (including NESTA and a people’s lottery).

We will clean up politics: end hereditary voting rights in the Lords; reform party funding and introduce Freedom of Information; incorporate the European Convention on Human Rights; devolve power to Scotland and Wales by referendum; create a London mayor and strategic authority; strengthen accountable local and regional government.

Britain will lead in Europe—reformist, not federalist—driving the single market, enlargement, CAP/CFP reform, openness, and signing the Social Chapter. Any entry to a single currency will be decided by the Cabinet, Parliament and the British people in a referendum, on economic merit. We will keep strong defence through NATO, retain Trident while pursuing multilateral disarmament, ban anti‑personnel landmines, and put human rights, development (towards the UN 0.7% target) and climate leadership at the centre of our foreign policy.

Britain deserves better—and with new Labour, Britain will be better.
